confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on aggregated 2026 cost-of-living data found through web search, converted from EUR to USD at about 1.10 USD per EUR. That rate comes from the RBA's 18 Nov 2026 AUD/USD rate of 0.6720 and AUD/EUR rate of 0.6115 as reported in the search summary. The figures used were: inexpensive meal about €15–17, cappuccino about €4.0–4.2, and 0.5 L domestic draught beer about €5.1–5.2, from the Numbeo-derived Expatica data, HousingAnywhere and MyLifeElsewhere. The mid-range meal for two is an estimate based on the usual ratio between inexpensive and mid-range meals in German cities (about €75). Cocktail (about €12) and wine (about €7) prices were not directly checked and are estimated from their usual relationship to local beer prices in Germany. All accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for July. I did not check them against live listings. Frankfurt hotel prices can rise sharply during trade fairs, so accommodation is the least certain part.
comparable_city_reasoning: Frankfurt prices are roughly 10–12% above the German average and close to Munich and Hamburg. Accommodation estimates use Frankfurt's role as a business and trade-fair city with a modest summer leisure peak.
